steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: There are three main aims of punishment: retribution (punishment because the offender deserves it), deterrence (putting people off committing crimes) and reformation/rehabilitation (helping the offender change their behaviour). | RS Exam Tips — Aims of Punishment: 1. For Aims of Punishment questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Aims of Punishment to its real-world impact on believers and society | UK Context: In the UK, debates about often involve both religious and secular voices. Pa

steps.body: Explain two aims of punishment and a religious view on each.
